property_summary: Invariant: After any single external Put(...) call by any user, the contract's recorded balance for that user equals the contract's Ether balance contributed in that call (i.e., Put always increases Acc[msg.sender].balance by msg.value exactly once); the mutant removing the nonReentrant guard allows a re-entrant attacker to cause Put to be executed multiple times in a single transaction and thus desynchronize recorded per-address balance from the actual single-call contribution, violating the invariant for some inputs.

For any single external Put call by an actor sending value V, the contract's recorded Acc[actor].balance increases by exactly V and equals the sum of prior recorded balance plus V after the call (reference enforces this via nonReentrant_ preventing reentrant double-execution; the mutant removing the guard allows a reentrant caller to reenter Put during the same transaction and cause Acc[actor].balance to be increased multiple times, breaking the rule for some inputs).

For any single external Put call by any actor sending some positive ETH, the reference contract's nonReentrant_ modifier prevents reentrant re-entry so that after Put returns the recorded per-address Acc[msg.sender].balance equals the amount added exactly once (i.e. it increased by msg.value once); the mutant that removes the guard can be re-entered by a malicious fallback to call Put again and cause Acc[msg.sender].balance to be increased multiple times, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any positive ETH value V (within balance bounds), a single external call to Put(V) always increases Acc[caller].balance by exactly V and leaves Acc[caller].balance equal to the sum of the prior stored balance plus V after the call in the reference (non-reentrant) contract; the mutant (with nonReentrant_ removed) can be re-entered by a malicious recipient during the same transaction to cause the stored balance to increase more than V, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any positive ETH value, a single external Put(...) invocation cannot result in Acc[caller].balance increasing by more than msg.value (reference enforces this via nonReentrant_; the mutant removes the guard allowing a reentrant attacker to cause multiple increments in one call and thus violate the rule).

After calling Put(unlockTime) by any sender with any value, the contract's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (reference enforces max(block.timestamp, _unlockTime)), but the mutant can set it to a past value when _unlockTime < block.timestamp, violating this property.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after Put(...) completes the stored unlockTime for that caller is never less than block.timestamp (reference uses max(block.timestamp, _unlockTime)); the mutant that sets acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make it < block.timestamp for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after Put(...) returns the stored unlockTime is either equal to the supplied _unlockTime when that is >= block.timestamp, or equal to block.timestamp when the supplied _unlockTime is < block.timestamp (i.e. acc.unlockTime == (_unlockTime > block.timestamp ? _unlockTime : block.timestamp)); the mutant that unconditionally assigns _unlockTime can leave acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, breaking this rule.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference ensures acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it never sets unlockTime to a past timestamp); the mutant can set unlockTime < block.timestamp when given a past _unlockTime, so we assert that Put never produces an unlockTime < block.timestamp.

For any caller, when Put is called with msg.value == 0 the reference preserves the previous unlockTime (does not regress it), while the mutant overwrites it with the supplied _unlockTime and can set it to an older value; thus for zero-value Put calls the stored unlockTime must remain unchanged.

After calling Put(x) the contract preserves any existing future unlockTime (i.e., Put only sets unlockTime to max(prev, block.timestamp) / does not lower it); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can lower a previously later unlockTime and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any input, calling Put(_) never decreases that caller's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime below its previous value (it sets unlockTime to max(previous, block.timestamp) in the reference); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease a previously set future unlockTime and thus violates this property for some inputs.

For any caller and any inputs, calling Put(...) never lowers that caller's stored unlockTime below its current value (i.e., Acc[caller].unlockTime after Put is >= Acc[caller].unlockTime before Put); the mutant that always resets unlockTime to block.timestamp can decrease a previously set future unlockTime and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime input, if the caller previously set a future unlockTime (> block.timestamp) then calling Put with an input >= that future unlockTime leaves the stored unlockTime unchanged (i.e., if caller had unlockTime T_prev > block.timestamp and calls Put(T_new) with T_new >= T_prev then after Put stored unlockTime == T_prev); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease it and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, if before calling Put the caller's stored unlockTime is <= block.timestamp then after Put the stored unlockTime equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp (it sets it to block.timestamp instead of _unlockTime).
A holder cannot Collect exactly at their unlockTime (Collect call should fail or not transfer) — i.e., Collect succeeds only when block.timestamp > unlockTime.
